articles.title: Modric plans to play for Croatia past 41st birthday
articles.summary: Luke Modric, 41, is not ready to retire from international football and hopes to play for Croatia in upcoming Nations League games, including against England.
body: Luka Modric turns 41 on Wednesday but is not ready to retire from international football just yet.

His decision coincides with the return of Slaven Bilic as manager, with the former West Ham boss helping to guide Modric's fledgling international career in his first stint in charge of the Croatia side, between 2006 and 2012.
Modric earned his first senior cap in March 2006, just before Bilic was named Croatia manager for the first time, and has since gone on to make 202 appearances for his country.
He was expected to call it a day after this summer's World Cup, when Zlatko Dalic's side were knocked out in the last 32 by Portugal.

articles.title: Pogacar will miss rest of season after Vuelta crash
articles.summary: Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar will not race again this season after suffering injuries including a fracture in his neck at the Vuelta a Espana.
body: The injury, which he suffered last month on the race's eighth stage, means the Slovenian will miss out on the chance to defend his title at the upcoming World Championships.
He crashed out of the Vuelta from a dominant position as race leader and required surgery on a broken collarbone, suffered a concussion, a "stable" fracture in his neck and multiple abrasions.

The 27-year-old, who was aiming to complete the set of Grand Tour titles, adding the Vuelta to his single Giro d'Italia victory and Tour de France wins, was due to defend his rainbow jersey at the World Championships in Montreal later this month.
"Of course, this isn't the way I wanted my season to finish," Pogacar said in a statement released by his team, UAE Team Emirates-XRG.

articles.title: FIA appeal court refutes Briatore impartiality claim
articles.summary: The FIA court of appeal refutes a claim by Alpine boss Flavio Briatore which it says "question the independence and impartiality of the judges".
body: Briatore claimed on Friday that one of the court of appeal judges in the case that ended with the court re-instating a penalty on Alpine's Pierre Gasly in the Monaco Grand Prix had "links" with McLaren.

The statement by the highest legal authority of motorsport's governing body said that court of appeal judges are "subject to the independence and confidentiality requirements contained in the FIA judicial and disciplinary rules, make annual disclosures of interests to the FIA compliance officer, and sign a specific declaration of independence for each particular case in consideration of the issue at stake and the parties involved".
It added that the parties to the dispute were invited both before and after the hearing "to raise any issues concerning the proceedings or the composition of the court. None did so".
It added: "No objection was raised during the hearing concerning the manner in which the court questioned the witness or conducted the proceedings.

Five minutes after the restart, Kiel took the lead with Adrian Kapralik’s brilliant strike, but Miroslav Klose’s men earned a point with an immediate equalizer by Piet Scobel, who has now scored in three successive away encounters.

Nürnberg’s winning start to the season came to an end, but they will remain top of the league unless Hertha BSC beat Magdeburg tomorrow afternoon. Kiel are still looking for their first league win of the season as three of their four games ended 2-2.

articles.title: Russell tops Hamilton at Monza ahead of qualifying
articles.summary: George Russell established himself as pole position favourite ahead of Italian Grand Prix qualifying as the Mercedes driver topped Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in final practice.
body: Mercedes and Ferrari had appeared closely matched in Friday's two practice sessions, and once more led the way on Saturday as Russell's time of 1:22.219s put him just over two tenths of a second clear of Hamilton at Monza.

Russell is shouldering Mercedes' hopes of claiming pole, with his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, serving penalties for taking new engine parts that will leave him starting from the back of the grid regardless of where he qualifies.

Despite being more focused on his long-run setup for Sunday's race, Antonelli, who leads both Russell and Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, was fourth behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
McLaren's Lando Norris, who has closed to within 83 points of Antonelli by winning the last two races, was fifth ahead of Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Face Salary Cap Decision Before Week 1
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions have a little financial housekeeping to handle before the 2026 regular season begins. Detroit currently has roughly $10.3 million in cap space under the NFL’s offseason top-51 accounting system, according to Over The Cap’s current Lions numbers.
body: Once full-season accounting takes effect, every player on the active roster counts against the cap, along with practice-squad contracts, injured players, PUP contracts and applicable dead money. Using those numbers, Pride of Detroit projects the Lions could be approximately $3 million over the cap when the accounting changes.
Detroit already restructured Jared Goff’s contract earlier this offseason, converting salary into signing bonus and creating approximately $32 million in 2026 cap room.
According to A to Z Sports’ breakdown of Detroit’s options, roughly another $14 million of Goff’s salary could potentially be converted, creating close to $12 million in additional 2026 cap space.
Penei Sewell and Amon-Ra St. Brown also have contracts Detroit could potentially restructure.
